title: Evaluate DeepSeek and Muse on held-out extraction tasks
objective: Model choice is based on correct accepted claims and review cost.
outcome: Independently adjudicated labels include critical-error categories and reviewer disagreement. Model output is not its own gold standard. Offline harness works without credentials. A live attempt reports exact model/endpoint and total spend without calling the network. A model failing a task class is disabled for that class. Neither cheap tokens nor inter-model agreement overrides the ≥0.98 precision / zero critical-error gate. Evaluation is reproducible from retained inputs/outputs. A failed model gate leaves deterministic collection operational.

commits.subject: Create independently adjudicated tasks
commits.instructions: Use representative CMS tables, CDC definitions, Census labels, units, date roles and deliberately insufficient evidence. Keep held-out labels outside implementer prompts.
commits.verification: Labels include critical-error categories and reviewer disagreement; model output is not its own gold standard.

commits.subject: Run paired bounded evaluation
commits.instructions: Compare the two exact model IDs with the same captured passages and output schema under a selected pilot budget. Save tokens, actual price, latency, abstentions and rejected claims.
commits.verification: Offline harness works without credentials; any live test reports exact model/endpoint and total spend.

commits.subject: Select the initial task-specific policy
commits.instructions: Report claim precision, useful coverage, critical errors and cost including review effort. Require ≥0.98 held-out precision and zero critical errors before routine publication eligibility.
commits.verification: A model failing a task class is disabled for that class; neither cheap tokens nor inter-model agreement overrides the gate.
